authority: Located construction/renewal comparison. No selected receiver, metal, support, joint, level or capacity.

location.disposition: Conditional garden test candidate; no site territory established

retainedBody.wetBody: One qualified continuous body between deliberate hydraulic/movement divisions; no selected length
retainedBody.proposedRestraint: Defined fixed datum near terminal, sliding seats elsewhere; exact design unproved
retainedBody.largerRepair: Qualified consumptive local repair or release of terminal/retainers and larger body renewal

separateTrays.mechanism: Individually watertight bodies with visible open transfers; not sealed ordinary laps

variables.zLip: Actual outlet-lip elevation of tray i, including offsets and sheet thickness
variables.ZWater: Governing downstream receiving-water elevation at transfer i
variables.g: Positive evidenced free separation; no selected value
variables.h: Non-negative downstream water depth above its entry floor
variables.F: Non-negative fall from each tray entry floor to its outlet lip
variables.Delta: Step from upstream outlet lip down to downstream entry floor
variables.D: Total available drop from first entry floor to last outlet lip

separateTrays.serialDrop: D = sum(F_i) + sum(Delta_i) >= sum(F_i) + sum(h_i+1 + g_i)
separateTrays.transferCount: n - 1 for a serial chain of n trays
separateTrays.rejection: For n > 1, zero available drop cannot accommodate positive free separations and non-negative falls/depths.
separateTrays.limit: Check actual lip/invert datums and permitted movement. A raised lip giving negative F lies outside this comparator; a local raised lip may still pond with positive F. The final lip-to-terminal gap and onward receiving drop lie outside D. Losing free separation under backwater invalidates this free-transfer claim, not every possible submerged gravity route.

sourceMechanisms.C11: CDA 10.3F: fixed soldered copper transverse seams for its watertight condition
sourceMechanisms.C12: CDA 10.5B: separately moving receiving gutter; 10.5C/D are different joined arrangements
